arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Friedlander argued the Ninth Circuit was wrong to call the error a structural defect.
Mr. O'Connell acknowledged the error is subject to the Brecht prejudice standard.
Mr. Shah argued the Court should hold the error is not structural and subject to harmless error review.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests how courts handle mistakes in jury instructions. One side argues the error is structural and voids the trial. The other side argues the error is harmless if it did not change the outcome.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute defines when courts must ignore jury instruction mistakes. It determines whether a flawed instruction automatically voids a trial or allows a verdict to stand if the mistake did not influence the jury's decision.
